rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says rulers need learned interpreters; the courtiers call the king’s single dream confused fragments to deny that it has a determinate meaning.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية ما يوجبه حال العلماء من حاجة الملوك إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dreams may be true inspiration from an angel, satanic confusion, or self-talk; the courtiers classify the king’s dream with the latter confused kinds.
rows.anchor: لأن الرؤيا تارة تكون من الملك وهي الصحيحة , وتارة تكون من تحريف الشيطان وتخليطاته , وتارة من حديث النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The courtiers use plural “dreams” for one dream to make it sound like meaningless fragments, then deny absolute expertise to conceal their ignorance.
rows.anchor: جمعوا - وهي حلم واحد - ليجعلوها أضغاثا لا مدلول لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the courtiers’ phrasing, negating knowledge without qualification also denies knowledge of this particular dream, after they have framed it as confused.
rows.anchor: ونفوا عن أنفسهم ( العلم المطلق ) المستلزم لنفي ( العلم بالمقيد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “said” entails recounting the actual words, whereas “spoke” does not necessarily quote what was said.
rows.anchor: فإذا ذكر أنه قال , اقتضى الحكاية لما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī derives the forms of ḥ-l-m from a common sense of diverting something from its accustomed course or nature.
rows.anchor: ومادة ( حلم ) بجميع تقاليبها تدور على صرف شيء عن وجهه وعادته وما تقتضيه الجبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer remembered Joseph after a long, accumulated span of time; “remembered” is parsed as a form meaning he sought remembrance.
rows.anchor: أي طلب الذكر - بالمعجمة , وزنه افتعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer confidently offers to report the dream’s interpretation and asks the court to send him to Joseph.
rows.anchor: { أنا أنبئكم } أي أخبركم إخبارا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Joseph “the truthful one” praises his exceptional truthfulness and his confirmation of what deserved belief, as the cupbearer had observed.
rows.anchor: أي البليغ في الصدق والتصديق لما يحق تصديقه بما جربناه منه ورأيناه لائحا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger repeats the seven cows and ears, using a plural form associated with small numbers for the count seven.
rows.anchor: وميز العدد بجمع السلامة الذي هو للقلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer’s “perhaps I may return” may express conventional caution about future events, regret and fear of an unwelcome interpretation, or urgency to hurry back.
rows.anchor: إما جريا على العوائد العقلاء في عدم البت في الأمور المستقبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He hopes the people will learn Joseph’s merit and what good or harm the dream portends, so they can act appropriately.
rows.anchor: ليكونوا على رجاء من أن يعلموا فضلك أو ما يدل ذلك عليه من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s interpretation predicts or commands seven years of sustained cultivation, corresponding to the fertile cows and ears in the dreams.
rows.anchor: فهو إخبار بمغيب , فهو أقعد في معنى الكلام , ويمكن أن يكون خبرا بمعنى الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāʾban means carrying on steadily according to a customary course, here with sustained effort.
rows.anchor: والدأب : استمرار الشيء على عادته

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Joseph gives useful advice suited to Egyptian wheat, which will not keep for two years unless preserved in its ears.
rows.anchor: بحسب طعام مصر وحنطتها التي لا تبقى عامين بوجه إلا بحيلة إبقائها في السنبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven severe years are famine years, represented by the lean cows and dry ears; their duration follows the two dreams’ imagery.
rows.anchor: { سبع } أي سنون { شداد } بالقحط العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famine years “eat” metaphorically through their inhabitants, consuming the grain previously stored for them.
rows.anchor: أسند الأكل إليهن مجازا عن أكل أهلهن تحقيقا للأكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reserve should last through the famine, with only a small amount kept outside storage for consumption.
rows.anchor: والإحصان : الإحراز , وهو إلقاء الشيء فيما هو كالحصن المنيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following year is a full twelve months; calling it ʿām signals that its coming relief is known and controlled by God alone.
rows.anchor: والتعبير به دون مرادفاته إشارة إلى أنه من المعلوم أنه لا يقدر عليها إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “People will be given rain” may derive from ghayth, rain, or “people will be relieved” from ghawth, deliverance; the first has three- and four-letter forms, the second only four-letter forms.
rows.anchor: ففي الأول يجوز بناءه من ثلاثي ومن رباعين يقال غاث الله الأرض وأغاثها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They will press” means extracting the juices and essences of things; pressing marks the transition from drought to fertility.
rows.anchor: { يعصرون } أي يخرجون عصارات الأشياء وخلاصاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph refuses to leave prison until the accusation is examined, seeking public vindication so his imprisonment is not taken as proof of serious guilt.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن السعي في براءة العرض حسن , بل واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph courteously alludes to the women’s plotting instead of naming the wife of the ʿAzīz, showing modesty and generosity.
rows.anchor: ولوح بمكرهن به ولم يصرح , ولا ذكر امرأة العزيز كرما وحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about what the king does not know is designed to spur investigation and secure acceptance of Joseph’s account once the truth is established.
rows.anchor: أخرج الكلام على سؤال عن علم ما لم يعلم يهيجه ويلهبه إلى البحث عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s insistence on clearing himself prevents the lasting shame and suspicion that could follow a prison sentence without public proof of innocence.
rows.anchor: وإن لم تظهر براءتي لم ينقطع عني كلام الحاسدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī defines kīd as scheming to cause harm.
rows.anchor: والكيد : الاحتيال في إيصال الضرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī distinguishes baliya, to wear out or perish, from ibtalā, to be afflicted, in this lexical survey.
rows.anchor: وبلى الشيء - بالكسر بلى مقصورا وبلاء ممدودا - إذا فنى وعطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several entries in the lexical survey are explained through an animal’s transformative contact with them.
rows.anchor: ولا ريب أن كلا من ذلك إذا خالطه الحيوان أحال حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī reads bāl as concern, thought, or worry, and explains “what is the matter?” through the idea of giving attention to another’s affair.
rows.anchor: والبال : الاكتراث والفكروالهم , ومن ذلك عندي : ما باليت به : لم أكترث به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wābil means very heavy rain with forceful impact and large drops.
rows.anchor: والوابل : المطر الكثير الشديد الوقع الضخم القطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king’s question about the women’s serious affair and the wording “when you solicited Joseph” show that his innocence was already recognized, though people were unsure which women had acted.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن براءته كانت متحققة عند كل من علم القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women evade the king’s question: “God forbid” and “we knew no evil of him” clear Joseph while leaving their own actions unconfessed.
rows.anchor: فأوهمن بذلك براءتهن منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their emphatic “no evil” makes Joseph’s innocence comprehensive; the court’s indirect speech also reflects fear of royal authority and a desire to leave room for evasion.
rows.anchor: وأعرقن في النفي فقلن : { من سوء } فخصصنه بالبراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife of the ʿAzīz admits that she pursued Joseph and confirms his truthfulness, after all the women have testified that he committed no wrong.
rows.anchor: شهد النسوة كلهن ببراءته , وإنه لم يقع منه ما ينسب به شيء من السوء إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaṣḥaṣ means the truth has become fully manifest and falsehood has withdrawn; Biqāʿī explains it through intensifying the root ḥ-ṣ-ṣ.
rows.anchor: أي حصل على أمكن وجوهه , وانقطع عن الباطل بظهوره

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives ḥaṣḥaṣ from ḥaṣṣ, cutting hair closely until what lies beneath becomes visible; al-Rummānī and al-Rāzī agree.
rows.anchor: ونظيره : كب وكبكب , وكف وكفكف , فهذه زيادة تضعيف , دل عليه الاشتقاق وهو قول الزجاج

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azharī offers another derivation: a camel’s calluses leave visible marks on the ground when it kneels.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري : هو من حصحص البعير : أثرت ثفناته في الأرض إذا برك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph recalls the brothers’ wrongs but attributes them to their ignorance at that earlier time, gently reminding them of the sin and prompting repentance.
rows.anchor: تلويحا لهم إلى معرفته وتذكيرا بالذنب ليتوبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By specifying the time of their ignorance, Joseph implies that they have since changed; his gentle words calm them as the revelation of his identity approaches.
rows.anchor: إفهاما لهم أنهم الآن على خلاف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers suspect his identity and ask emphatically whether he is Joseph; the author says the exchange was apparently without an interpreter.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا كان بغير ترجمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph identifies himself and Benjamin as brothers, then says God has favored them by reuniting them in a good state.
rows.anchor: بأن جمع بيننا على خير حال تكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qunbul retains the final yāʾ of yattaqi in both forms, treating the verb like a sound verb to signify complete, constant piety.
rows.anchor: وأثبت قنبل - بخلافه عنه - ياءه في الحالين معاملا له معاملة الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā means warding off harm by following guidance, and patience means restraining the self while enduring the bitterness of denied desire.
rows.anchor: والتقوى : دفع البلاء بسلوك طريق الهدى ؛ والصبر : حبس النفس بتجرع مرارة المنع عما يشتهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph reveals himself gradually to avert panic, prevent renewed treachery, and let the brothers recognize his justice and forgiveness before bringing Jacob to Egypt.
rows.anchor: ليظهر لهم إحسانه وعدله ودينه وخيره , وكفه عنهم وعفوه عن فعلهم بالتدريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph specifies this shirt to distinguish it from the bloodied one; its ordinary use makes its healing effect more wondrous and signals his faith and religious integrity.
rows.anchor: وكونه قميصا من ملابس يوسف المعتادة أدخل في الغرابة وأدل على الكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shirt is especially fitting as a sign of grace because a shirt is closest to the body and represents religion in dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: والقميص ألصق الثياب بالجسم , فإظهار الكرامة به أدل على كمال دين صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says Judah carried the bloodied shirt before and now carried this one to bring Jacob joy; he went barefoot and bareheaded for eighty farsakhs.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان يهوذا هو الذي حمل قميصه لما لطخوه بالدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan had left al-ʿArīsh, the last Egyptian town toward Syria, when Jacob strongly affirmed that he could smell Joseph’s scent.
rows.anchor: من العريش آخر بلاد مصر إلى بلاد الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s “if you did not think me senile” means he is stating his perception despite expecting disbelief; tafnīd is accusing an old person of failing judgment.
rows.anchor: أي لقلت غير مستح ولا متوقف , لأن التنفيذ لا يمنع الوجدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī explains fasalat as leaving a place, wijdān as perception that rules out nonexistence, and scent as what the nose detects.
rows.anchor: والوجدان : ظهور من جهة إدراك يستحيل معه انتفاء الشيء , والريح : عرض يدرك بحاسة الأنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers swear that Jacob remains in his old error, meaning his persistent belief that Joseph is alive.
rows.anchor: أي خطئك في ظن حياة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s promise to install the believers in the land after their oppressors encourages them; they prevail while every arrogant opponent fails.
rows.anchor: فاستبشروا بذلك الوعد من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿInād is knowingly refusing the truth out of pride and oppression; jabbār is blameworthy in a servant because it seeks an ultimate rank that belongs to God.
rows.anchor: والعناد : الامتناع من الحق مع العلم به كبرا وبغيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell lies ahead of the arrogant denier as his unavoidable destination, and ṣadīd is the discharge of the people of Hell, including pus and blood.
rows.anchor: وهو غسالة أهل النار كقيحهم ودمائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinner swallows the foul drink only with great effort, in small gulps, because of its bitterness and heat; swallowing it means letting it pass through the throat.
rows.anchor: يتكلف بلعه شيئا فشيئا لمرارته وحرارته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death-like causes beset him from every direction, but God keeps him alive so the punishment continues; another severe punishment awaits afterward or on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: لأنا قضينا بدوام حياته زيادة في عذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers’ good deeds are like ash scattered by a violent wind: charity, freeing slaves, and ransoming captives yield them nothing at Judgment because the deeds lack a foundation.
rows.anchor: بل ذهب هباء منثورا لبنائه على غير أساس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable also evokes a traveler whose route misleads him into remote ravines where he cannot remain or return, so he perishes lost.
rows.anchor: فأبعد كل البعد حتى وصل إلى شعاب لا يمكن فيها المقام

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya, with al-Ḥawfī, allows a second parsing in which “their deeds” is a new subject whose predicate also completes the first clause.
rows.anchor: كما قال الحوفي وابن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sūrat al-Naḥl aims to establish God’s complete power and knowledge, free choice, and transcendence above every imperfection; the bee is its clearest sign.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على أنه تعالى تام القدرة والعلم ، فاعل بالاختيار ، منزه عن شوائب النقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bee’s precise skill in building, foraging, and producing varied honey, including healing honey despite consuming diverse fruits, displays divine blessing and power.
rows.anchor: من دقة الفهمة في ترتيب بيوتها ورعيها وسائر أمرها

rows.speaker: ابن ميلق
rows.claim: Ibn Milq, transmitting exegetes, describes Arab infanticide: a newborn girl could be buried alive by her mother’s husband, while a boy was welcomed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن ميلق : قال المفسرون : كانت المرأة إذا أدركها المخاض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source says female infanticide occurred among Muḍar, Khuzāʿa, and Tamīm.
rows.anchor: وكان الوأد في مضر وخزاعة وتميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their judgment is vile because they assign to God what they dislike while reserving for themselves what they prefer, despite receiving every blessing from Him.
rows.anchor: بجعل ما يكرهونه لمولاهم الذي لا نعمة عندهم إلا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disbelieve in the afterlife receive the “evil likeness” of weakness, need, humiliation, and foolishness; God alone has the highest likeness of perfection.
rows.anchor: من الضعف والحاجة والذل والرعونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty, with no peer or impediment, and wise, placing everything correctly; immediate judgment would empty the earth of people.
rows.anchor: الذي لا يمتنع عليه شيء فلا نظير له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God punished people immediately for their wrongdoing, no creature would remain: creatures are either culpable or depend on human life, as in the time of Noah.
rows.anchor: لأن الكل إما ظالم يعاقب بظلمه , وإما من مصالح الظالم فيهلكه عقوبة للظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ẓulm includes actual and latent shirk; the reciprocal form of “take to account” conveys especially thorough reckoning.
rows.anchor: وكان الشرك - الذي هذا سياقه - أظلم الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “on it” covers every creature on earth or within it, making this formulation broader than the wording in Sūrat Fāṭir.
rows.anchor: عبر بما يشمل كل محمول الأرض سواء كان على الظهر أو في البطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God delays people mercifully and wisely until a term fixed from eternity; once it arrives, they cannot delay or advance it by even an hour.
rows.anchor: إمهالا بحكمته وحلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says balā can affirm after a negative statement, unlike naʿam, and can answer a negative sentence even when no question was asked.
rows.anchor: وتأتي ( بلى ) في النفي من غير استفهام , يقال : ما أعطيتني درهما , فنقول : بلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wabāl is severity and a bad outcome, associated with heaviness; the related wabīl can mean harsh punishment or an unpalatable pasture.
rows.anchor: والوبال : الشدة وسوء العاقبة , وهو من الشدة والثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibil is a collective singular rather than a plural or collective noun, and the same form can mean clouds carrying rain.
rows.anchor: والإبل : السحاب الذي يحمل ماء المطر , وهو ظاهر في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī explains the many camel-related derivatives through the transformative effect of contact, riding, and carrying.
rows.anchor: الإحالة في خلطتها بالركوب والحمل وغيرهم واضحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s four chief aims are theology, prophecy, the afterlife, and divine decree with free choice; theology is the foremost, and the signs also prove resurrection.
rows.anchor: تقرير أصول أربعة : الإلهيات , والنبوات , والمعاد , وإثبات القضاء والقدر والفعل بالاختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain, snow, or hail revive dry land by God’s will, just as He revives human bodies after death and souls through knowledge after ignorance.
rows.anchor: فيعلمون أنه ينزل من أمره ما يريده فيحيي به أجساد العباد بعد موتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For people who hear” signals that this clear sensory proof needs receptive listening and submission, not extensive speculation; “see” would wrongly suggest a need for deep reflection.
rows.anchor: ولعله لم يختمها ب ( يبصرون ) لئلا يظن أن ذلك من البصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock milk is a sign because it is purified from dung, blood, and other admixtures and remains easy to drink.
rows.anchor: موضع العبرة تخليص اللبن من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce nusqīkum with ḍamma, from asqā (providing drink); Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim in Shuʿba’s transmission pronounce it with fatḥa, from saqā (giving a drink).
rows.anchor: وبالفتح في قراءة نافع وابن عامر وعاصم في رواية شعبة : من سقاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anʿām is a collective noun treated as masculine singular; the masculine pronoun in “its bellies” is unambiguous because the milk comes from females.
rows.anchor: فكان مفردا كما نقل ذلك سيبويه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that fodder in the animal’s rumen separates into dung below, milk in the middle, and blood above; the liver distributes them to their respective places.
rows.anchor: إذا أكلت البهيمة العلف واستقر في كرشها طبخته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farṯ is the heavy material that descends to the rumen and ceases to be called farṯ once it leaves; sāʾigh means easy passage through the throat.
rows.anchor: وهو الثقيل الذي ينزل إلى الكرش , فإذا خرج منه لم يسم فرثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse distinguishes intoxicating drink, which blocks reason and is blameworthy, from wholesome provision such as vinegar and date syrup, which harms neither body nor mind.
rows.anchor: ذا سكر منشيا مطربا سادا لمجاري العقل قبيحا غير مستحسن للرزق

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ibrāhīm, al-Shaʿbī, Abū Razīn, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and Qatāda that intoxicating drink is the prohibited beverage and wholesome provision is lawful drink.
rows.anchor: قيل : السكر ما حرم من الشراب , والرزق الحسن : ما أحل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpreters who take “sukr” to mean intoxicant say its permissibility was abrogated by the prohibition in Sūrat al-Māʾida; the wording already signals disapproval.
rows.anchor: ومن حمل السكر على السكر قال : إنها منسوخة بآية المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sukr” has four lexical senses: intoxicant, food, stillness, or the verbal noun for intoxication, whose root suggests blockage of channels.
rows.anchor: والسكر في اللغة على أربعة أوجه : الأول ما أسكر . الثاني ما أطعم من الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses iḥtibāk: mentioning “sukr” implies its opposite in the second phrase, while “good provision” implies the first item’s negative quality.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر السكر أولا دال على الفتح ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī argues the verse supports the Muʿtazilite view that rizq can include unlawful things.
rows.anchor: فالآية أدل ما في القرآن على المعتزلة في أن الرزق يطلق على الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life passes through infancy and growth, youth, maturity with declining strength, and old age with obvious weakness; some die in strength while others reach decrepitude.
rows.anchor: مذكرا بمراتب عمر الإنسان الأربع , وهي سن الطفولية والنمو , ثم سن الشباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The frailest age returns a person to childlike weakness and can bring loss of knowledge, with no medicine or remedy able to avert it; people should reflect before it arrives.
rows.anchor: فيصير إلى مثل حال الطفولية في الضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing the preposition before “anything” makes ignorance encompass the entire period after knowledge, continuing until death.
rows.anchor: نزع الخافض للدلالة على استغراق الجهل لزمن ما بعد العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge and power encompass all things: whatever He wills occurs, and His power can prevent what He knows will not occur.
rows.anchor: فمهما أراد كان , ومهما أراد ولم يرده هو , أحاط به علمه
